core_condition: at least one measured effect recorded in observed_effects from Ventora telemetry or public corpora

evidence.rationale: Two bundled phenomena with uneven robustness. Framing (Tversky & Kahneman 1981; Levin's typology of risky/attribute/goal framing) is reliable, attribute framing especially. Anchoring (Tversky & Kahneman 1974) is real for explicit and self-generated anchors, and Maniadis, Tufano & List (2014, AER) provide evidence it replicates — but the incidental/subliminal anchoring variants were part of the replication crisis and are weaker or unreliable. Score 2 reflects that this L1 bundles a solid component (framing, explicit anchoring) with contested variants (incidental anchoring); we lead with the robust versions.

product_applicability.rationale: Central to pricing pages and plan selection — a top-priority Ventora conversion surface. Price anchoring, tier structure, gain/loss framing all directly implementable. Reference at scale: SaaS 3-tier pricing, Apple pricing order, insurance framing.

measurability.rationale: Maps to cvr, average_plan_value, tier_selection_distribution, frame A/B CVR — all Amplitude-reachable and A/B-testable.

orthogonality.rationale: Bundles two distinct cognitive phenomena (framing, anchoring) into one L1 for product coherence — both are presentation-of-choice effects at the pricing/selection funnel point. Some overlap with LA-01 (loss framing) and SC-06 (scarcity framing), documented in relations. Score 2 reflects the deliberate bundle and managed overlap.

safety.rationale: When anchors are real and framing is truthful, this is standard, legitimate value presentation. Risks — fake 'was' prices, fabricated anchors, deceptive decoys, misleading framing — are blocked by hard rules and are directly regulated (EU Omnibus price-reduction rules, FTC deceptive pricing). The boundary is clear and legally well-defined, hence 3 with strong guardrails.

dissent: Anchoring was a focal point of the replication crisis. While classic explicit anchoring (Tversky & Kahneman 1974) and self-generated anchoring replicate well, several incidental and subliminal anchoring findings failed to replicate or showed much smaller effects than originally reported. Maniadis, Tufano & List (2014) specifically re-examined anchoring reliability and argued the core effect survives, but the episode disciplines our claims: we use explicit, real anchors (genuine higher tiers, true prior prices) — the robust variant — and do not rely on incidental/subliminal anchoring. Framing effects are more consistently replicated but also vary by type (attribute framing strongest); we lead with attribute and gain/loss framing over weaker goal-framing claims.

evidence_sources.ref: Tversky & Kahneman (1981). The Framing of Decisions and the Psychology of Choice. Science 211(4481).
Tversky & Kahneman (1974). Judgment under Uncertainty: Heuristics and Biases. Science 185(4157).

Levin, Schneider & Gaeth (1998). All Frames Are Not Created Equal: A Typology of Framing Effects. OBHDP 76(2).
